items.explanation: Sliding-filament theory states that force comes from myosin cross-bridges walking on actin, not from shortening of the filaments themselves. The A band is the thick-filament array and keeps its length; the I band (thin filaments not overlapping myosin) and H zone (thick filaments not overlapped by actin) shrink as overlap increases and Z-lines approach. Constant measured filament lengths in the stem rule out myosin-spring models and titin hydrolysis as the shortening engine. Titin is an elastic linker, not a fuel that is cleaved each stroke.

distractor_rationales.A: A-band length is the thick filament length and remains constant during physiologic shortening.
distractor_rationales.B: Z-lines move closer together in contraction, not apart.
distractor_rationales.C: Titin is not consumed as a hydrolyzed fuel to shorten thick filaments.

items.stem: A point mutant of cardiac troponin C has a 10-fold higher Kd for Ca2+ (lower affinity) with no change in myosin ATPase kcat measured on unregulated thick filaments. At a given systolic cytosolic Ca2+, active force is expected to:

choices.text: Increase, because tropomyosin will be permanently displaced from actin
Be unchanged, because force is set only by myosin kcat, which was not altered
Fall, because occupancy of TnC Ca2+ sites drops, so less tropomyosin movement and fewer available cross-bridge sites
Fall only if the SR calcium-release channel is a proteolytic fragment of TnC

items.explanation: Thin-filament activation begins when Ca2+ binds troponin C, moving tropomyosin and exposing myosin-binding sites on actin. Fractional occupancy of a binding site is Ca / (Ca + Kd). Raising Kd tenfold at the same [Ca2+]i lowers occupancy, so less tropomyosin shift, fewer attached bridges, and less force. Myosin's unloaded kcat on unregulated filaments can be normal because the lesion is regulatory, not in the myosin catalytic core. Lower affinity does not lock tropomyosin off actin. RyR is a separate SR protein, not a TnC fragment.

distractor_rationales.A: Weaker Ca2+ binding reduces, not permanently increases, thin-filament activation.
distractor_rationales.B: Force in the sarcomere is gated by the troponin-tropomyosin switch even when myosin kcat is intact.
distractor_rationales.D: TnC affinity does not need RyR proteolysis to change force; the occupancy effect is sufficient.

items.stem: A parathyroid adenoma secretes excess PTH. Serum Ca2+ is high and phosphate is low. PTH raises Ca2+ in part because it:

choices.text: Binds osteoblasts, increasing RANKL expression that activates osteoclasts, and also increases renal Ca2+ reabsorption and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D production
Directly binds osteoclasts as its only receptor-bearing bone cell, with no effect on kidney or vitamin D
Blocks renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase and thereby lowers intestinal Ca2+ absorption as the cause of hypercalcemia
Is identical to calcitonin and inhibits osteoclasts, which paradoxically raises serum Ca2+

items.explanation: PTH receptors on osteoblasts (and osteocytes) induce RANKL, which binds RANK on osteoclast precursors and increases bone resorption, releasing Ca2+ and phosphate. Simultaneously PTH increases distal-tubule calcium reabsorption, decreases phosphate reabsorption (explaining hypophosphatemia), and stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase to make 1,25-(OH)2D, which increases intestinal Ca2+ absorption. Osteoclasts lack the classical PTH receptor; the osteoblast relay is the MCAT-relevant point. Calcitonin, from thyroid C cells, opposes resorption. Blocking 1-alpha-hydroxylase would lower, not raise, gut Ca2+ uptake.

distractor_rationales.B: PTH acts on osteoblasts to control osteoclasts via RANKL, and it has major renal/vitamin D actions.
distractor_rationales.C: PTH stimulates, rather than blocks, 1-alpha-hydroxylase; hypercalcemia is not from less vitamin D.
distractor_rationales.D: Calcitonin lowers serum Ca2+; PTH is not calcitonin.

items.stem: A child with vitamin D deficiency has low intestinal Ca2+ and phosphate absorption, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and poorly mineralized osteoid at growth plates (rickets). The organic matrix that fails to mineralize adequately is composed primarily of:

choices.text: Hydroxyapatite crystals with no protein scaffold
Glycogen granules secreted by osteoblasts
Pure elastin, which is the tensile protein of bone osteoid
Type I collagen osteoid, which normally nucleates hydroxyapatite mineral

items.explanation: Bone is a composite: type I collagen and ground substance (osteoid) deposited by osteoblasts, later mineralized with hydroxyapatite. In rickets/osteomalacia the scaffold is laid down but calcium-phosphate product is insufficient for proper mineralization, so unmineralized osteoid accumulates and bones are soft. Hydroxyapatite is the mineral, not the organic matrix. Elastin is important in ligaments and skin, not the bulk of bone osteoid. Glycogen is not the secreted bone matrix. Vitamin D's role here is mineral supply (and PTH-driven wasting of phosphate), not a switch from collagen to elastin.

distractor_rationales.A: Hydroxyapatite is the missing mineral, not the organic osteoid that is overabundant in rickets.
distractor_rationales.B: Osteoblasts do not build osteoid from glycogen.
distractor_rationales.C: Bone tensile protein is type I collagen, not elastin.

items.stem: In a hot environment, cutaneous vasodilation and sweating increase heat loss. Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors on eccrine sweat glands and sweating stops, although skin blood flow remains high. Core temperature is then more likely to rise because:

choices.text: Radiative heat gain from vasodilation always exceeds any other term when atropine is present
Shivering is the primary heat-loss mechanism and atropine triggers it
Evaporative cooling of sweat is impaired, removing the main avenue of heat loss when air temperature approaches or exceeds skin temperature
The epidermis becomes an infinite water-permeability barrier only after muscarinic blockade

items.explanation: When ambient temperature is near or above skin temperature, convection and radiation cannot dump heat and may even add heat. Evaporation of hypotonic eccrine sweat then becomes the critical cooling term. Those glands are sympathetic but cholinergic (muscarinic) at the neuroglandular junction, so atropine produces anhidrosis and heat storage. Vasodilation still delivers heat to the skin but cannot evaporate it without sweat. Shivering is a heat-gain response to cold. Atropine does not create a tighter stratum corneum; if anything, the problem is too little surface water, not an infinite barrier.

distractor_rationales.A: Vasodilation can still lose heat if a gradient exists; the atropine-specific defect is evaporation.
distractor_rationales.B: Shivering produces heat; it is not a cooling mechanism activated by atropine.
distractor_rationales.D: Muscarinic blockade stops sweat secretion; it does not suddenly waterproof the epidermis as the reason temperature rises.

items.stem: A full-thickness burn destroys epidermis including the stratum corneum. Insensible water loss and infection risk both rise sharply. The most direct explanation is loss of:

choices.text: Dermal melanin production, which is the primary water-tight seal of skin
The cornified lipid-keratin barrier that limits transepidermal water loss and microbial invasion
Vitamin D photoproduction, which is what physically occludes bacteria
Eccrine overproduction of hypotonic fluid as the only change after a burn

items.explanation: The stratum corneum is a brick-and-mortar of keratinized corneocytes and intercellular lipids from lamellar bodies. That composite is the principal barrier to evaporative water loss and to many microbes. Destroying it in a full-thickness burn is why patients desiccate and become infected unless the surface is replaced or dressed. Melanin absorbs UV in deeper living layers; it is not the water seal. Cutaneous vitamin D synthesis is a photochemical reaction, not a mechanical lid on bacteria. Burned skin does not cool the patient by secreting extra sweat from destroyed glands; insensible loss is barrier failure, not eccrine overdrive.

distractor_rationales.A: Melanin is a UV pigment transferred to keratinocytes, not the lipid-keratin water barrier.
distractor_rationales.C: Vitamin D is a hormone precursor, not the physical occlusion that keeps water in and pathogens out.
distractor_rationales.D: Full-thickness injury destroys sweat glands; the water loss is passive through a missing barrier.
